Commissioner Hetherington recognized the strong turnout at the September 11th Remembrance Ceremony at Charlie Leighton Park and the walk over to Veteran's Memorial Park. She expressed hope that the community will move forward in a spirit of unity.\par
\par
Vice Chair Ciampi echoed Commissioner Hetherington's comments and noted that approximately 3000 people participated in the walk. He thanked PAL, Martin County Fire Rescue, and Martin County Sheriff's Office for their efforts. He also recognized The House of Hope's record breaking, 400 foot Cuban sandwich event at Justin Wilson Park. Vice Chair Ciampi extended birthday wishes Sarah [Derek Powell's wife] and recognized his 35th wedding anniversary and his parents' 66th wedding anniversary.\par
\par
Chair Heard thanked the Fire Department and Sheriff's Office for their contributions to the 9/11 ceremony. She recognized a sixth grade student's electric guitar performance of The Star-Spangle Banner and invited him to perform at a Board meeting. She discussed water quality improvements made over the past two years, including muck removal and burning activities at Lake Okeechobee by the SFWMD and FWC. Chair Heard also referenced a discussion with Nick Musia regarding their project to remove phosphorus from the lake and the ribbon cutting ceremony for the C23 and C44 interconnect pump station. She also referenced Governor Desantis' statements regarding $10 billion invested in water quality improvements.\par
\par
Commissioner Capps highlighted the 9/11 Bridge Walk and encouraged residents to participate. He also discussed the yellow roadway signs announcing developments and requested stronger language identifying developments mandated by the State, such as the Baron Landings and Cove Road projects. He suggested language identifying state mandated, administratively approved projects, and state authorized agricultural enclaves.\par
\par
Commissioner Vargas expressed concerns regarding drivers' ability to safely read development signs and supported clearer information. She reported attending the 9/11 bridge walk and pump station ribbon cutting ceremonies. Commissioner Vargas encouraged residents to attend the 5:05 budget public hearing.\par
